headline: 12 + Israel National News/Israel Realtime) -- IDF at highest readiness / leave frozen ahead of Oct 27 election
dek: APA reports the Israeli military raised readiness to its highest level and deployed tens of thousands of troops ahead of the Oct 27 election, with strengthened security around Gaza, the Lebanese border, the West Bank and Jerusalem, heightened air-defence readiness against possible missile attacks…
sources: APA (citing IDF/military statement); Israel National News (Zamir leave orders); Israel Realtime (IDF drill announcement); Haaretz Oct 19 (leave freeze + no specific threat)
fault_line: Election security or election theatre -- is the army locking the country down against a real threat, or staging readiness to help the incumbent?

sections.what_happened: APA reports the Israeli military raised readiness to its highest level and deployed tens of thousands of troops ahead of the Oct 27 election, with strengthened security around Gaza, the Lebanese border, the West Bank and Jerusalem, heightened air-defence readiness against possible missile attacks from Iran or Lebanon, and all land border crossings closed on election day. Israel National News reports IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir ordered leave restrictions, increased commander presence and additional deployments, and cancelled leave on election day amid fears of Iranian/proxy escalation. Israel Realtime reports the IDF announced a preplanned exercise simulating a multi-front attack for Sunday and Monday in northern and central Israel (Air Force, Northern and Central Commands), rehearsing surprise attack and infiltration scenarios. COUNTERPOINT: Haaretz (Oct 19) reported the leave freeze but also that the defence establishment had identified no escalation in threats and no specific intelligence of an imminent attack, and Israel Realtime notes the IDF said the drill was planned in advance with 'no concern over a security incident'.
sections.what_verified: Posture measures corroborated across APA, Israel National News and Israel Realtime; Haaretz (T3) corroborates the leave freeze and supplies the no-specific-threat counterpoint
sections.what_disputed: Haaretz Oct 19: IDF sources said no specific threat was identified ahead of the election and no call-up orders issued; the drill is preplanned, not a response to new intelligence. Netanyahu's repeated pre-election warnings of enemy attacks are his claims, not the defence establishment's assessment.
sections.why_matters: Tens of thousands of troops, leave cancelled, a multi-front drill on Sunday and Monday -- and the army itself says there is no specific threat. Two days before the vote, Israel is on its highest alert for an enemy its own generals cannot name.
sections.context: Background: NEW to scans (missed catch-up, APA 07:12 + Israel National News/Israel Realtime) -- IDF at highest readiness / leave frozen ahead of Oct 27 election; preplanned Sun-Mon multi-front drill in north and central Israel

totw_analysis: Our read: Tens of thousands of troops, leave cancelled, a multi-front drill on Sunday and Monday -- and the army itself says there is no specific threat. Two days before the vote, Israel is on its highest alert for an enemy its own generals cannot name. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Election security or election theatre -- is the army locking the country down against a real threat, or staging readiness to help the incumbent?
